source.title: Replay What Matters: Off-Policy Replay for Efficient LLM Reinforcement Unlearning
source.authors: Zirui Pang; Chenlong Zhang; Haosheng Tan; Zhuoran Jin; Jiaheng Wei; Zixin Zhong

page_placements.theme: Prompt variants leave more residual than direct queries, in settings or metrics E's verdicts did not count

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates post-unlearning forgetting and retained utility for RULE and its replay variant on benchmark tasks, but does not test the recovery attacks central to the broader claim.
record.gate_note: The reported results are ordinary post-training benchmark evaluations, not tests of recovery by relearning, activation editing, quantization, or prompting. They do not compare outcomes with a stated chance level. Table 1 is flattened and its values are not assigned here because the layout does not reliably map all values to models and metrics.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper. ReRULE is a training-efficiency add-on to RULE, and the study reports only standard post-unlearning forget and utility scores for its own method against baselines. It runs no relearning, activation-editing, quantization or prompting recovery attack and makes no chance-level comparison, so it does not test whether the forgetting is shallow or robust. Version A's defining part, that simple attacks don't recover the knowledge, is never tested. ReRULE is not presented or tested as attack-resistant (F).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that replaying low-reward hard cases improves the efficiency of RL unlearning and Retain Quality (MUSE 46.3 to 56.2) at 5–11% extra training time. Gains are limited on the easy TOFU forget01 split. They also claim a tighter theoretical hard-case convergence bound, and attribute RULE/ReRULE's results to learning refusal rather than erasing knowledge.
record.recipe_differences: ReRULE retains RULE's initial refusal SFT and adds a hard-case replay buffer with importance-sampled off-policy updates during later GRPO training.
record.method_sensitivity: Replay threshold changes the hard-case selection and reported MUSE outcomes; the authors say including easier samples can reduce performance.

fits_no_version.finding: On RWKU (Llama3-8B-Instruct), the benchmark's adversarial-attack (AA) forget probes leave higher ROUGE than plain QA probes. ReRULE scores AA 33.2 vs QA 13.1; RULE scores AA 38.3 vs QA 16.8; the original model scores AA 74.7. The scores come from a flattened Table 1 and are not framed as a recovery test.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-based RL unlearning leaves more residual knowledge under adversarial benchmark probes than under direct QA probes.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors state RULE and ReRULE succeed by learning precise refusal rather than erasing knowledge. This is an assertion with no analysis behind it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-trained unlearning blocks access rather than deleting (version C), asserted without a test.

record.problems: The study does not test recovery attacks or report a chance-level comparison. Reported results have no uncertainty estimates. The TOFU table is flattened, so its method-to-value mapping is not fully clear.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 RWKU results and other baseline-method scores were omitted because the flattened layout does not reliably assign all reported values to the corresponding method and metric. MUSE refusal-naturalness scores were omitted because they do not measure retained general ability or targeted-knowledge recovery.

untested.parts: Near-chance accuracy and resistance to simple recovery attacks. Only standard post-training forget and utility metrics are reported.
No activation ablation or analysis of whether knowledge is blocked or deleted.
No targeted prompting recovery attack. Only the RWKU benchmark's built-in adversarial probes are scored.
ReRULE is not evaluated against any recovery attack.

missing.what: RWKU forget-probe ROUGE by probe type (FB/QA/AA) for RULE and ReRULE against the original model, including the adversarial-attack probes
missing.versions: E (indirect; benchmark adversarial probes, not a recovery attack)

record.verdict_notes: Method/efficiency paper with no recovery attacks, so no verdicts are given. Table 8 values for the threshold ablation were mis-assigned in the record: ReRULE0.6 = 6.6/1.3/52.3 and ReRULE1.0 = 4.3/1.4/53.7 (Verb/Know/Utility). The RWKU base model is Llama3-8B-Instruct; MUSE and TOFU use Llama2-7B. The appendix describes RWKU 'AA' inconsistently, as both adversarial attack and author attribution. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study evaluates forgetting and retained utility, but does not establish near-chance accuracy or test whether simple attacks recover knowledge.
No post-unlearning relearning or fine-tuning attack is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of whether knowledge is blocked rather than deleted is tested.
No prompt-rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery attack is tested.
ReRULE is an unlearning-training method, but the study does not test its resistance to the recovery attacks listed in the claim.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: One untested remark: RULE/ReRULE succeed by learning refusal 'rather than directly erasing knowledge'. Plus a general ethics note on residual memorization. No test.

tranche.reason: Method paper. It reports only its own method's standard forget and utility scores against baselines. RWKU AA probes are built into the benchmark and averaged into Forget Quality, not run or analysed as a recovery attack. No relearning, activation, quantization or robustness claim, so not T2 or F.

source_check.notes: No rows or verdicts. The only near-test datum is RWKU's AA forget column (Table 1, Llama3-8B-Instruct), which the synthesis files under unfit. MUSE and TOFU results use Llama2-7B. The test_reason's 'no prompting recovery attack' should note that RWKU's built-in adversarial probes are reported.

statements.correction: Table 1 (Llama3-8B-Instruct, RWKU, GRPO variants): ReRULE QA 13.1, AA 33.2; RULE QA 16.8, AA 38.3; original QA 70.3, AA 74.7. Forget ROUGE-L, lower is better forgetting. The authors do not discuss the AA-QA gap.
statements.problem: None. Table 1 is flattened, but the cells place by the row averages (RULE 28.0/16.8/38.3, All 27.7; ReRULE 26.5/13.1/33.2, All 24.2). Context: the original model also scores AA above QA (74.7 vs 70.3), and the gap widens after unlearning.
